verses.text: There was a man named Job who lived in the land of Uz. He was a good man with no fault in him. He was honest, he respected God, and he stayed away from evil.
He had seven sons and three daughters.

He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys. He also had a very large number of servants. He was the greatest man among all the people of the East.
Job's sons took turns holding feasts in their homes, each on his special day. They would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

When the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children and make them clean before God. He would get up early in the morning and offer a burnt offering for each of them. Job thought, "Maybe my children have sinned and turned against God in their hearts." Job did this every time.
One day the angels came to stand before the LORD, and Satan, the accuser, came with them.
The LORD asked Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From wandering around the earth, going back and forth across it."
Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him. He is a good man with no fault in him. He is honest, he respects God, and he stays away from evil."
Satan answered the LORD, "Does Job respect God for no reason?
You have put a wall of protection around him, his family, and everything he owns. You have blessed everything he does, and his flocks and herds have spread all over the land.
But reach out your hand and take away everything he has, and he will curse you to your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "All right. Everything he has is in your power, but do not lay a finger on Job himself." Then Satan left the LORD's presence.
One day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at the home of their oldest brother.
A messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys were eating grass nearby.
Then the Sabeans attacked and took them away. They killed the servants with swords, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you!"
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "Fire from God fell from the sky. It burned up the sheep and the servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you!"

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three groups, attacked the camels, and took them away. They killed the servants with swords, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you!"
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
Suddenly a strong wind blew in from the desert and hit the four corners of the house. It fell on the young people, and they are dead. I am the only one who escaped to tell you!"
Then Job got up and tore his robe and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped.
He said, "I had nothing when I was born, and I will have nothing when I die. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Praise the name of the LORD."
In all this, Job did not sin or blame God for doing wrong.
